reviews.title: Sparkful IG & X pages not updated for almost a year, and I can’t find a way to contact them directly
reviews.text: I have had the Walkr app since it was first released under Fourdesire, and it was managed pretty well. I was somewhat concerned when Sparkful took over the app, but overall, they seem to have made some positive changes and improvements to the app. However, I have been having a very difficult time trying to find a way to contact Sparkful directly. When I went to their IG and X pages, I found that neither of them have been updated for almost a year, so that was of no help to me. I do not have a Facebook account, so I don’t know if their page on there has been updated since last year or not. That being said, I have yet to find a way to contact Sparkful directly. I am hoping that posting this 1 star review will get their attention and they will reply.

reviews.title: Genuinely good motivation
reviews.text: If you enjoy meeting goals or crossing things off lists but make it fun, this is a good way to motivate yourself into getting more steps. The missions are like a list to check off but it only works when you find the right planets during exploring. Exploring and building and upgrading all take an increasing amount of time, money, and cubes and to speed it up you walk. You unlock more ways to help yourself using steps to generate currency as you progress so it keeps the small incremental motivations coming as the game progresses and the only thing a subscription would add is more things to walk and spend energy and coins on so I’m personally waiting on that because there’s so much to do even without it. If it works for your brain then it really works.

reviews.title: Would be fun… if it weren’t for that energy cap.
reviews.text:
Tried it… after 3 days, I deleted it.  

That cap of 10k energy instead of a more flexible 100% energy for 24h just kills it for me as I’m walking 15-20k steps a day and only open it at night.

Otherwise it just turns into yet another thing I have to manage on its time instead of at my own schedule.

reviews.title: Used to be fun
reviews.text:
Playing for many years and as time wears on so does the game. Increasingly longer timeframes for goals, fewer regional participants, virtually no [human] tech support, less interest.
Update 7.26. Way over a decade in now and whomever is developing this app is not paying attention to details (prob using AI). Buy into subscription with little expectation. Bright, shiny new planets that take more than a month, or all of your stored energy to get to, are a distraction to all the little glitches. Operates on the level of a college lab

reviews.title: Fun, not too time consuming, and rewarding
reviews.text:
Pros:
* Simple enough while still being fun.
* Encourages exercise.
* Very cute with the planet types, the food maker (DFR) types, the ships you continue to collect, and more!
* Cute game music.
* Continually being updated by active developers.

Cons:
* Can be a little battery intensive since it's always trying to track your steps.

Overall, really enjoying this app as a good game that you can play daily without sinking huge hours.
